title: H05 Holdout: an answer arrives, with and without a cue to which matter it belongs
capability: Holdout counterpart of the older-natural-continuation class. Two things are awaiting an answer: a request for a growing plot made over three months ago and a request to try out for a singing group made this week. A bare announcement that an answer has come cannot be attributed, so a light clarification is right and neither guessing the recent one nor asking for the whole story again is. Two days later, after talk of digging and of a posted letter from a committee, the same kind of sentence does carry a cue and should be connected to the old request.

allowed.statement: Both a place on the waiting list for a growing plot and a request to try out for the community singers' winter performance are waiting for an answer.
The letter is about the growing plot the person signed up for in July, for which the organisers were to write by post once one came free.

forbidden.statement: Taking the bare announcement to be about the singing group without checking.
Taking the bare announcement to be about the growing plot without checking.
Asking the person to explain from the beginning what they had asked or signed up for.
Connecting the posted letter to the singing group despite the digging context, the post and the word used for the senders.
Stating or implying whether a plot has been offered; what the letter says has not been told.

expectedBehavior: Bare announcement: share the excitement and ask which one, naming both in a few words.
Cued announcement: recognise it as the answer about the plot and ask what it says, without inventing the outcome.
Never ask for the back story again.
failureSignals: The old request never reaches the Provider when the cue points at it.
The bare announcement is silently attributed to the most recent matter.
The cued announcement still triggers a clarification or is attributed to the singing group.
